newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet sowings nearly complete - planters.
newsitem.headline: French beet sowings nearly complete - planters.

text.p: French farmers said on Wednesday they hoped to complete sugar beet sowings by the end of this week or early next week, having already drilled 90 percent of area.
"Weather conditions are very good and sowings may be over by the end of the week or early next week," an analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.

As of April 2 sowing operations were one or two days ahead of last year, he said. Dry weather over the last 10 days helped farmers make good progress in the fields but there were now worries over continued lack of rainfall.
"What the crop needs at this stage is some rain," he said.
Sowings were now complete in Burgundy and in the south of Paris and nearly complete in Normandy.
In the north, area sown to sugar beets stood at around 95 percent in the Picardie region, 80 percent in the Nord-Pas-de Calais region and 95 percent in the Oise, Somme and Aisne regions.
In the east planted area was 70 percent in the Ardennes, Marne and Alsace regions.
France produced 4.23 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1996/97.
